# Apple revenue and gross margin, FY2021–FY2025

## Conclusion

Over five fiscal years, revenue grew 13.8%, from $365.817B to $416.161B. Gross margin rose 5.13 points, from 41.78% to 46.91%. The segment data in the 10-K shows that most of the gain since FY2023 came from Services: its gross margin rose from 70.8% to 75.4%, while Products only moved from 36.5% to 36.8%.

## Data

In billions of US dollars. Gross margin is calculated from the values in the table.

| Fiscal year | Ended | Revenue | Gross profit | Gross margin |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FY2021 | 2021-09-25 | 365.817 | 152.836 | 41.78% |
| FY2022 | 2022-09-24 | 394.328 | 170.782 | 43.31% |
| FY2023 | 2023-09-30 | 383.285 | 169.148 | 44.13% |
| FY2024 | 2024-09-28 | 391.035 | 180.683 | 46.21% |
| FY2025 | 2025-09-27 | 416.161 | 195.201 | 46.91% |

Segment gross margin from Item 7 of the FY2025 10-K:

| | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Products | 36.5% | 37.2% | 36.8% |
| Services | 70.8% | 73.9% | 75.4% |

## Analysis

- Revenue fell 2.8% in FY2023, then grew for two years in a row.
- The FY2025 10-K attributes the lower Products margin mainly to product mix and tariff costs.
- The same filing says Apple expects gross margins in general to face volatility and downward pressure.

## Limitations

- FY2023 had 53 weeks and the other years had 52, which slightly affects year-over-year comparisons.
- Segment margins only cover FY2023 to FY2025. Earlier years weren't read.
- This sample was fetched on 2026-11-03, when the latest annual report on EDGAR was FY2025.
